subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR's internal yielding glob walker and bootstrap-hook interleaving changes as the scoped fix for the embedded_run bootstrap-context stall before broader Gateway worker/offload work?
rationale: The code path and tests look sound, but the PR intentionally changes compatibility-sensitive internal scheduling and traversal semantics used by plugin hooks and bootstrap context loading.

options.title: Accept the scoped mitigation
options.body: Merge after maintainer review and green exact-head gates, treating the traversal and hook interleaving changes as acceptable internal behavior for protecting Gateway availability.

options.title: Require connected runtime proof
options.body: Ask for an embedded_run/channel proof that shows keepalives or cheap Gateway work proceed during bootstrap before accepting the scheduling change.

options.title: Defer to broader architecture work
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers prefer worker isolation, caching, or priority scheduling instead of changing current bootstrap traversal and hook scheduling.

recommendation.title: Accept the scoped mitigation
recommendation.body: Merge after maintainer review and green exact-head gates, treating the traversal and hook interleaving changes as acceptable internal behavior for protecting Gateway availability.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest history-backed owner for the bootstrap read and internal hook architecture affected by the merge-risk decision.
